forces.title: AI-enabled underwriting and claims driven by DPI data
forces.description: India's digital public infrastructure (Aadhaar, UPI, Account Aggregator, ABHA, DigiLocker, Bima Trinity) provides a unique foundation for AI-led transformation in financial services. Insurers can leverage consent-based data from AA and ABHA to support AI-enabled underwriting, pre-assessing risk and flagging information. In claims, AI can combine ABHA-linked records, DigiLocker documents, and claims history for automated triage and validation, driving demand for advanced data services.
forces.source_title: India’s new insurance track: The marathon becomes an AI-led decathlon

forces.title: B2B digital ecosystem to drive data-led credit underwriting
forces.description: India is developing an interoperable digital layer to digitize the B2B order-to-cash cycle, functioning as a secure information exchange rail. This will reduce information asymmetry and enable buyer-confirmed invoices to become financeable records, shifting credit underwriting from collateral to cash flow. This infrastructure will be compounded by advanced analytics and generative AI for cash-flow intelligence, dynamic risk scoring, and agentic credit underwriting, fundamentally changing the data needs for credit assessment and opening new avenues for data and research providers.
forces.source_title: India’s Next Growth Frontier: B2B Commerce, Payments, and Credit

forces.title: AI to drive demand for advanced financial analytics
forces.description: The financial services sector is at an inflection point due to the convergence of AI, tokenization, and quantum technologies. AI is increasingly driving efficiencies in customer acquisition, underwriting, fraud detection, servicing, and collections. This necessitates advanced analytical capabilities and data processing, creating a strong tailwind for financial data providers and research firms who can supply AI-ready data, models, and specialized insights to financial institutions seeking to unlock AI's full potential for growth and cost compression.
forces.source_title: Balance: Thriving in the Age of AI

forces.title: Government platforms enhancing data availability for financial services
forces.description: India's digital infrastructure stack, including platforms like Account Aggregator (AA), Data.gov.in, and AIKosh, is significantly enhancing data availability for financial services. AA provides a consent-based framework for sharing financial data, Data.gov.in offers machine-readable public datasets, and AIKosh serves as a repository for AI models and sandbox resources. These initiatives create robust foundational data layers, enabling data providers and research firms to access diverse, verified information for analysis and decision-making, driving innovation in financial products.
forces.source_title: India’s Next Growth Frontier: B2B Commerce, Payments, and Credit

forces.title: AI transforming financial analyst workflows and productivity
forces.description: Artificial Intelligence, particularly Generative AI, is poised to significantly transform financial analyst workflows, leading to substantial productivity gains and cost compression. AI can reduce compliance costs by running KYC, AML, and fraud detection processes at machine speed. Crucially, it can compress tasks like credit memo generation, document generation, and risk analysis to minutes, freeing analysts from prep and research. This shift necessitates data and research providers to integrate AI-powered tools and offer AI-ready data solutions to support this enhanced productivity in financial institutions.
forces.source_title: Balance: Thriving in the Age of AI

forces.title: India's DPI creating rich real-time financial data ecosystems
forces.description: India's Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI), including UPI, DigiLocker, Account Aggregators (AAs), and Aadhaar, is creating one of the world's richest real-time financial data ecosystems. UPI processes over 18 billion transactions monthly, providing an immense volume of granular transaction data. This vast and accessible data pool forms a foundational layer for AI-driven underwriting, financial inclusion, and hyper-personalized banking, presenting a significant tailwind for financial data providers who can leverage this resource to develop innovative products and services.
forces.source_title: Beyond automation: How AI is reshaping the next decade of banking

forces.title: Data portability via Account Aggregator and ULI transforming finance
forces.description: The Account Aggregator (AA) framework and Unified Lending Interface (ULI) are fundamentally transforming financial services by making verified information portable and credit decisions more contextual. With nearly 2.9 billion financial accounts enabled through AA-based data sharing, these platforms facilitate the movement of finance from isolated transactions to coordinated outcomes. This increased data portability directly impacts financial data providers and research firms, requiring them to adapt to new data access paradigms and develop services that leverage these interconnected data flows.

forces.title: Generative AI enhancing cyber threats to financial data
forces.description: The increasing adoption of Generative AI (GenAI) significantly expands the cybersecurity threat landscape for financial institutions and data providers. GenAI enables attackers to generate highly convincing phishing campaigns, automate vulnerability detection, and execute social engineering at an unprecedented scale and near-zero marginal cost. This poses a critical risk to the integrity and security of financial data, requiring data providers and research firms to invest heavily in advanced cybersecurity measures, fraud detection, and data sovereignty to protect their valuable information assets.
forces.source_title: Beyond automation: How AI is reshaping the next decade of banking

forces.title: India's sovereign AI development boosts domestic data and analytics
forces.description: India is actively building sovereign AI capabilities through substantial investments in infrastructure, talent, and innovation, exemplified by 15,200 datasets on AIKosh and significant semiconductor investments. This national strategy aims to strengthen domestic AI and semiconductor ecosystems, fostering competitiveness and resilience. This development provides a strong tailwind for Indian financial data and research providers, who can leverage these indigenous resources and datasets to develop AI-native financial services, offering faster decisions and more personalized experiences while reducing reliance on foreign technology.

forces.title: Finance to become AI-operating system by 2030
forces.description: The global financial services industry is undergoing a structural transformation, with AI projected to become its core operating system by 2030, influencing over 80% of operations within autonomous multi-cloud ecosystems. This shift is expected to deliver significant benefits, including 40-60% cost reductions, 30-50% shorter cash conversion cycles, 70-90% faster decision-making, and 60-80% improved forecast accuracy. This profound change implies massive demand for AI-ready data, advanced analytics, and specialized research models, fundamentally reshaping the offerings of data and research providers.

forces.title: Open finance expanding access to customer-owned financial data
forces.description: Open finance initiatives are fundamentally reshaping the financial services landscape by expanding access to financial data beyond traditional banking, fostering more connected and personalized customer experiences. The proliferation of consent-based data portability and interoperable frameworks is accelerating ecosystem-led innovation, directly enabling the creation of new data-driven services and business models. This structural shift is highly beneficial for financial data and research providers, as it increases the availability and interoperability of valuable customer data for analysis and product development.

viewpoints.title: Digitizing business information is next growth frontier for India
viewpoints.description: India’s next growth frontier lies in digitizing business information flows, mirroring the success of UPI and Aadhaar for population-scale participation. By extending trusted connective digital infrastructure to the business economy, commerce can scale easier, supply chains become responsive, and capital can follow economic activity. This reduces information asymmetry, strengthens supply-chain resilience, and improves access to working capital, enabling more informed commercial and credit decisions, which will drive demand for specialized data providers.
viewpoints.source_title: India’s Next Growth Frontier: B2B Commerce, Payments, and Credit

viewpoints.title: India poised to lead in intelligent, sovereign, and scalable financial systems
viewpoints.description: India is uniquely positioned to lead the development of future-ready financial operating systems by combining intelligence, trust, and scale. The convergence of AI, trusted data, programmable money, and digital public infrastructure (like Aadhaar, UPI, Account Aggregator) is creating an environment for autonomous and inclusive financial services. This positions India to build an architecture with embedded intelligence, sovereign capabilities, and resilience, which is a positive outlook for local financial data and research providers driving these foundational elements.

viewpoints.title: Accelerating AI adoption in banking and capital markets
viewpoints.description: While only 26% of organizations have transitioned AI initiatives from pilots to enterprise-wide production, confidence in AI's future remains high, with widespread adoption expected to accelerate in the next year. Banking and capital markets are projected to be at the forefront of this expansion, indicating a significant shift towards AI-driven operations. This accelerating adoption signals a strong and continuous demand for AI-ready data, advanced analytical tools, and specialized research capabilities from data and research providers to support this industry transformation.

demand_drivers.driver: Demand for alternative data and AI-driven credit scoring
demand_drivers.description: AI is breaking down structural barriers to provide credit to underserved segments by leveraging alternative data. This includes UPI transaction history, geospatial signals, satellite imaging for farm intelligence, digital footprint, and even computer vision from asset photographs or self-portraits to build comprehensive borrower and asset risk scores. This drives significant demand for specialized data aggregation, alternative data products, and AI-powered analytical solutions from financial data and research providers.

demand_drivers.driver: Expanding capital markets and investor participation
demand_drivers.description: India's capital markets are experiencing significant growth, with stock market-linked accounts exceeding 21 crore and demat accounts reaching over 18 crore. India has also climbed to the fifth spot in global market capitalization rankings. This surge in retail and institutional investor participation, coupled with a robust IPO pipeline, drives increased demand for high-quality financial data, market research, and independent ratings to inform investment decisions, support regulatory compliance, and enable sophisticated analysis in an expanding market.

new_opportunities.description: The upcoming B2B interoperable layer will enable consent-based sharing of verified invoice, payment, and financing records. This forms a trusted data foundation for cash-flow, credit, and risk intelligence. Leveraging advanced analytics and AI, financial service providers can develop agentic credit underwriting systems to assess working capital in near real-time against verified invoice flows, extending collateral-free credit, and generating supplier/buyer risk scoring, which is a new opportunity for data and analytics providers.

The B2B interoperable digital layer has the potential to generate aggregated, anonymized rail activity into real-time, economy-wide trade signals. This provides unprecedented visibility into economic activity. Financial data providers and research firms can leverage this granular, dynamic data to offer advanced open-market intelligence, helping businesses and investors make more informed decisions, identify trends, and anticipate market shifts, representing a significant new service offering.

market_sizing.methodology: Analysis of new service opportunities arising from enhanced digital infrastructure and AI capabilities.
